## Purpose and package shape
This is a Haskell implementation of the Ouroboros consensus family, packaged as five libraries: core consensus, protocol extensions, Cardano-era integration, node diffusion, and an LSM LedgerDB backend. The Cabal component graph is rooted at `ouroboros-consensus.cabal`; primary source packages are `ouroboros-consensus/`, `ouroboros-consensus-protocol/`, `ouroboros-consensus-cardano/`, and `ouroboros-consensus-diffusion/`.

## Entry points and composition
The reusable node assembly surface is core node startup/protocol information in:
- `ouroboros-consensus/src/ouroboros-consensus/Ouroboros/Consensus/Node/Run.hs`
- `ouroboros-consensus/src/ouroboros-consensus/Ouroboros/Consensus/Node/ProtocolInfo.hs`
- `ouroboros-consensus-diffusion/src/ouroboros-consensus-diffusion/Ouroboros/Consensus/NodeKernel.hs`

Cardano binds concrete Byron/Shelley-family eras and their hard-fork sequence into the generic framework:
- `ouroboros-consensus-cardano/src/ouroboros-consensus-cardano/Ouroboros/Consensus/Cardano.hs`
- `ouroboros-consensus-cardano/src/ouroboros-consensus-cardano/Ouroboros/Consensus/Cardano/Node.hs`
- `ouroboros-consensus-cardano/src/ouroboros-consensus-cardano/Ouroboros/Consensus/Cardano/Ledger.hs`

Standalone operational entry points are ChainDB tools under `ouroboros-consensus-cardano/app/`, notably `db-analyser.hs`, `db-synthesizer.hs`, `immdb-server.hs`, and `snapshot-converter.hs`.

## Consensus and era boundary
Generic block, ledger, protocol, ticking, and header-validation abstractions isolate consensus from a particular blockchain:
- `ouroboros-consensus/src/ouroboros-consensus/Ouroboros/Consensus/Block.hs`
- `ouroboros-consensus/src/ouroboros-consensus/Ouroboros/Consensus/Ledger/Abstract.hs`
- `ouroboros-consensus/src/ouroboros-consensus/Ouroboros/Consensus/Protocol/Abstract.hs`

The hard-fork combinator lifts blocks, ledger states, transaction handling, forging, protocol rules, serialisation, and queries across eras. Era transition/history logic is a key boundary between time/configuration and era-specific validation:
- `ouroboros-consensus/src/ouroboros-consensus/Ouroboros/Consensus/HardFork/Combinator.hs`
- `ouroboros-consensus/src/ouroboros-consensus/Ouroboros/Consensus/HardFork/Combinator/Translation.hs`
- `ouroboros-consensus/src/ouroboros-consensus/Ouroboros/Consensus/HardFork/History.hs`

## Block-to-chain state flow
Received or forged blocks pass protocol/header validation and ledger application, then ChainDB chooses and persists the selected chain. ChainDB coordinates immutable, volatile, and ledger-state stores; it exposes followers, iterators, and query paths to networking and local clients:
- `ouroboros-consensus/src/ouroboros-consensus/Ouroboros/Consensus/Storage/ChainDB/API.hs`
- `ouroboros-consensus/src/ouroboros-consensus/Ouroboros/Consensus/Storage/ChainDB/Impl.hs`
- `ouroboros-consensus/src/ouroboros-consensus/Ouroboros/Consensus/Storage/ChainDB/Impl/ChainSel.hs`

Persistence is split deliberately: immutable on-disk chunks, volatile recent blocks, and rollback-capable ledger-state sequences/snapshots:
- `ouroboros-consensus/src/ouroboros-consensus/Ouroboros/Consensus/Storage/ImmutableDB.hs`
- `ouroboros-consensus/src/ouroboros-consensus/Ouroboros/Consensus/Storage/VolatileDB.hs`
- `ouroboros-consensus/src/ouroboros-consensus/Ouroboros/Consensus/Storage/LedgerDB/V2.hs`

## Transaction, forging, and protocol paths
The mempool admits transactions against a ledger snapshot, sequences them under capacity policy, and updates/revalidates on chain changes; forging consumes its current validated transaction view:
- `ouroboros-consensus/src/ouroboros-consensus/Ouroboros/Consensus/Mempool/API.hs`
- `ouroboros-consensus/src/ouroboros-consensus/Ouroboros/Consensus/Mempool/Update.hs`
- `ouroboros-consensus/src/ouroboros-consensus/Ouroboros/Consensus/Block/Forging.hs`

Protocol families include BFT/PBFT in core plus Praos/TPraos in the protocol and Shelley/Cardano layers:
- `ouroboros-consensus/src/ouroboros-consensus/Ouroboros/Consensus/Protocol/PBFT.hs`
- `ouroboros-consensus-protocol/src/ouroboros-consensus-protocol/Ouroboros/Consensus/Protocol/Praos.hs`
- `ouroboros-consensus-cardano/src/shelley/Ouroboros/Consensus/Shelley/Protocol/Praos.hs`

## Network and client boundaries
Mini-protocol implementations translate peer activity into ChainDB and mempool operations: Chain Sync exchanges headers/rollbacks, Block Fetch transfers bodies, and local protocols provide state queries and transaction submission. Diffusion wires those protocol implementations into node-to-node and node-to-client connections:
- `ouroboros-consensus/src/ouroboros-consensus/Ouroboros/Consensus/MiniProtocol/ChainSync/Client.hs`
- `ouroboros-consensus/src/ouroboros-consensus/Ouroboros/Consensus/MiniProtocol/BlockFetch/Server.hs`
- `ouroboros-consensus-diffusion/src/ouroboros-consensus-diffusion/Ouroboros/Consensus/Network/NodeToNode.hs`

CBOR wire/disk compatibility is a material external contract, specified for Cardano node-to-node and storage formats in `ouroboros-consensus-cardano/cddl/`.

## Runtime and infrastructure
The runtime is Haskell with STM/concurrency abstractions and filesystem-backed databases; Nix and Cabal provide reproducible builds (`flake.nix`, `cabal.project`). Key external ecosystem dependencies include `io-sim`/`io-classes`, `fs-api`/`fs-sim`, and `lsm-tree`. The optional LSM LedgerDB backend is isolated at `ouroboros-consensus/src/ouroboros-consensus-lsm/Ouroboros/Consensus/Storage/LedgerDB/V2/LSM.hs`. Formal Agda specifications live independently in `docs/agda-spec/`.
